title: Progressive schema migrator and soft coercion pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a progressive schema migration service in the ingestion path to allow safe evolution of usage event shapes without bulk consumer breakage. The service will: negotiate schema versions using a header/version tag, apply 'soft coercion' rules for non-breaking coercions (string->enum normalization, numeric parsing, optional field fill), route strongly incompatible events to a quarantine stream for human review, and emit rich validation telemetry. Goal is to reduce manual rollbacks and SDK churn when producers land small shape changes.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress accepts events stamped with schema v1,v2,v3 and applies transformation rules documented in Confluence
Soft coercion rules implemented as a small rule DSL and unit-tested with >90% coverage
Quarantine stream created in Kafka topic 'telemetry-quarantine.v1' with automated sample messages and owner tags
End-to-end test harness validates canary traffic (5% rollout) for 72h without degradation of ingest latency >10%
Observability: per-schema rejection rate, coercion counts, and sample mutation diffs visible in Console dashboard
comments: 2026-02-26 - Aisha: RFC posted in Confluence (see links). Initial design proposes a lightweight rule DSL and library that can be reused in Private deployments.
2026-03-02 - Tomás: Spike complete for rule DSL prototype. Prototype handles enum normalization and numeric coercion; parsing edge-cases around ISO timestamps require clarifying product behaviour.

2026-03-05 - PM Mariah Liu: Product decision: prefer silent coercions for optional fields but quarantine if required fields change type. Added acceptance criteria for quarantine topic and sample retention policy.

2026-03-08 - Eng review: Chose to implement coercion as a composable middleware that can run in ingest workers or as a separate transform layer. Trade-off: slightly higher p99 latency if run inline; mitigation: fast-path for known-good schemas and asynchronous enrichment for low-priority mutations.
2026-03-10 - Tomás: Implemented canary routing (5%) and new metrics emitted to telemetry. Opening PR for review: GitHub PR #5123.
2026-03-12 - Security: Reviewed data flow; no plaintext PII introduced by coercion step. Security review not required for this change per checklist. We'll still log mutations for auditability.
